outline.chapter_title: Orientation to Federal Firearms Prosecutions and Sentencing
outline.description: Introduces the federal framework governing felon-in-possession offenses and the sentencing architecture that frequently accompanies them, setting the doctrinal stage for using United States v. Cutbank as a teaching vehicle.
subtopics: Statutory core: 18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(1) (felon-in-possession) and § 924(e) (ACCA)
Typical proof problems in possession cases (actual vs. constructive possession; identification of the firearm)
The Sentencing Guidelines’ role post-Booker: advisory ranges and district court discretion
Recurring evidentiary disputes in firearms trials: propensity, hearsay, confrontation, and Rule 403
Appellate review overview: evidentiary abuse of discretion, harmless error, procedural vs. substantive reasonableness

outline.chapter_title: Elements of § 922(g)(1): Status, Possession, Knowledge, and Commerce
outline.description: Details the elements the government must prove to convict under § 922(g)(1), including developments after Rehaif and practical trial considerations.
subtopics: Elements: (1) prior felony status; (2) knowing status at time of possession (Rehaif); (3) knowing possession; (4) interstate commerce nexus
Proof of status and knowledge of status after Rehaif and Greer (plain-error posture when unpreserved)
Possession: actual, constructive, and joint possession; evidentiary indicia (DNA, eyewitness identification, proximity, conduct)
Interstate commerce: minimal nexus sufficiency
Indictment and jury instruction patterns for § 922(g)(1)

outline.chapter_title: Second Amendment Challenges to Felon Disarmament After Bruen
outline.description: Places felon-in-possession prosecutions in the post-Bruen Second Amendment landscape with an emphasis on Eighth Circuit doctrine.
subtopics: Bruen’s history-and-tradition test and its application to status-based prohibitions
Eighth Circuit approach upholding § 922(g)(1) against facial challenges (e.g., United States v. Jackson)
As-applied challenges by non-violent felons: circuit splits and trends
Strategic considerations: preserving Second Amendment objections in § 922(g)(1) cases

outline.chapter_title: Proving Possession: Intrinsic Evidence vs. Rule 404(b) Propensity
outline.description: Explains when prior-acts evidence is intrinsic to the charged offense of possession and when it is governed by Rule 404(b), with the Cutbank court’s use of prior possession of the same firearm as a focal example.
subtopics: Intrinsic evidence doctrine: completing the story, same transaction/series, continuous possession
Rule 404(b) basics: permitted non-propensity uses; Huddleston admissibility framework
Eighth Circuit precedent: prior possession of the same firearm as intrinsic evidence (United States v. Battle)
Continuous possession as a theory to link earlier sightings to the charged offense
Rule 403 balancing overlay even for intrinsic evidence; limiting instructions under Rule 105

outline.chapter_title: Hearsay, Non-Hearsay Uses, and the Confrontation Clause in Police-Response Testimony
outline.description: Covers how out-of-court statements are used to explain police conduct without violating hearsay rules and the Confrontation Clause, with attention to sequencing testimony and limiting instructions.
subtopics: Defining hearsay and non-hearsay purposes (effect on listener, background/context)
Crawford-Davis line: testimonial vs. non-testimonial statements; primary-purpose test
Confrontation satisfied when the declarant appears for cross-examination (e.g., Charboneau)
Managing trial flow: whether to preclude early reliance on declarant statements before declarant testifies
Appellate review of limiting-instruction decisions (abuse of discretion; adequacy of end-of-trial instructions)

outline.chapter_title: Rule 403 and the ‘Opening the Door’: Context, Emotion, and Prejudice
outline.description: Analyzes Rule 403 balancing and the doctrine of ‘opening the door’ when cross-examination elicits emotionally charged context, using the testimony about a victim’s family member’s death as a case study.
subtopics: Rule 403: unfair prejudice, confusion, waste of time vs. probative value
Opening the door: fairness after impeachment and contextual rehabilitation
Managing emotional or victim-impact-adjacent facts during the guilt phase
Remedies and safeguards: striking, curative instructions, scope limitations
Standard of review: broad trial court discretion (e.g., Sprint/United Mgmt. Co. v. Mendelsohn)

outline.chapter_title: Impeachment with Prior Inconsistent Statements: Rule 613, Authentication, and Police Reports
outline.description: Unpacks Rule 613(b)’s requirements for using extrinsic evidence of inconsistent statements and the authentication hurdles when the ‘statement’ is embedded in a police report authored by someone else.
subtopics: Rule 613(a)-(b): foundation requirements and extrinsic proof
Authentication under Rule 901: who can authenticate; adoption by the witness
Police reports: hearsay problems and authorship; limits of reading from reports
Alternative routes: recorded recollection (Rule 803(5)), prior sworn testimony (Rule 801(d)(1)(A)), public/business records (Rules 803(6), 803(8)) and their constraints
Eighth Circuit’s insistence on authentication before admitting extrinsic impeachment (e.g., United States v. Cumbie)

outline.chapter_title: Limiting Instructions: Timing, Content, and Strategy
outline.description: Explores when limiting instructions are required, the permissibility of end-of-trial instructions in lieu of contemporaneous ones, and strategic considerations for both parties.
subtopics: Rule 105 and the court’s discretion to defer limiting instructions
When contemporaneous instructions are advisable to prevent misuse
Drafting precise instructions for intrinsic evidence, non-hearsay purposes, and impeachment-only uses
Preservation, requests, and standards on appeal
Risks of over-emphasis and jury confusion

outline.chapter_title: Harmless Error and Cumulative Error in Criminal Appeals
outline.description: Provides the frameworks for assessing whether evidentiary or instructional errors warrant reversal, distinguishing constitutional from non-constitutional error and addressing cumulative-error claims.
subtopics: Non-constitutional harmless error: ‘substantial and injurious effect’ / ‘substantially swayed’ standard
Constitutional harmless-error standard: harmless beyond a reasonable doubt
Cumulative-error doctrine: aggregation and the requirement of substantial prejudice
Burden allocation and record-driven analysis
Application in firearms trials with strong physical and testimonial evidence

outline.chapter_title: Guidelines for Firearms Offenses: The § 2K2.1 Framework
outline.description: Maps the structure of USSG § 2K2.1 from base offense levels to specific offense characteristics commonly triggered in felon-in-possession cases.
subtopics: Base offense levels tied to prior convictions and weapon type (including firearms described in 26 U.S.C. § 5845(a), such as sawed-off rifles/shotguns)
Specific offense characteristics: altered/obliterated serial number (§ 2K2.1(b)(4)(B)), number of firearms, stolen firearm, trafficking
Cross-references and interaction with other chapters (e.g., § 3C1.2 reckless endangerment during flight)
Relevant conduct and uncharged behavior at sentencing
Evidentiary standards at sentencing: preponderance and reliance on undisputed PSR facts

outline.description: Focuses on the four-level enhancement for using or possessing a firearm ‘in connection with’ another felony, including the Eighth Circuit’s approach and commentary definitions.
subtopics: Text and commentary: potential to facilitate and embolden; not requiring a separate charge or conviction (comment. n.14(A), n.14(C))
Common contexts: drugs (fortress theory), assaults, burglaries, domestic offenses, flight from police
Causation and nexus: temporal and spatial proximity; facilitation vs. mere presence
Standards of proof and review: preponderance at sentencing; clear-error review for factfinding; de novo for legal interpretation
Practical proof: using victim testimony, physical evidence, and undisputed PSR narratives

outline.chapter_title: ACCA and the Armed Career Criminal Guideline (§ 4B1.4): Interaction and Calculations
outline.description: Explains how a § 924(e) finding changes the Guidelines analysis, including offense level selection and automatic criminal history category, and how it interacts with § 2K2.1.
subtopics: ACCA predicates: ‘violent felony’ after Johnson’s residual-clause invalidation; enumerated and elements clauses (overview)
Guideline mechanics under § 4B1.4: offense level alternatives and automatic Criminal History Category VI
Choosing the greater offense level when § 2K2.1 and § 4B1.4 both apply
Charging practice vs. sentencing reality: jury findings on ACCA and judicial factfinding for enhancements
Illustration: when § 2K2.1 enhancements push above the ACCA default offense level

outline.chapter_title: Procedural and Substantive Reasonableness: Gall, Rita, and Eighth Circuit Presumptions
outline.description: Surveys the post-Booker appellate framework for reviewing sentences, emphasizing correct Guidelines calculation, consideration of § 3553(a), and the presumption of reasonableness for within-Guidelines sentences in the Eighth Circuit.
subtopics: Procedural reasonableness: correct range, responding to arguments, adequate explanation (Gall; Rosales-Mireles)
Substantive reasonableness: abuse-of-discretion review of length; Rita’s appellate presumption
Eighth Circuit applications: presumption for within-range sentences (e.g., Goodhouse) and treatment of preserved mitigation (e.g., Masood; Maluoth)
Building a record: articulating § 3553(a) factors and variances
Common pitfalls: miscalculations vs. disagreements with policy

outline.chapter_title: United States v. Cutbank as a Teaching Vehicle
outline.description: Connects the general doctrines to the court’s analysis in Cutbank, showing how evidentiary rulings and sentencing decisions were affirmed under the Eighth Circuit’s standards.
subtopics: Intrinsic evidence of prior possession of the same sawed-off rifle: reliance on Battle; continuous possession rationale
Police-response testimony: non-hearsay context and Confrontation satisfied because declarant testified
Rule 403 and opening the door: allowing rehabilitative context about victim’s aversion to guns
Impeachment via police reports: authentication required for extrinsic proof; permissible scope of cross-examination
Harmless and cumulative error: strong physical (DNA, recovery path) and testimonial evidence foreclosing prejudice
§ 2K2.1(b)(6)(B) enhancement: use ‘in connection with’ another felony established via undisputed PSR; standard of review
Guidelines calculation vs. ACCA guideline: higher § 2K2.1-driven level controls over § 4B1.4 default
Within-Guidelines sentence affirmed: presumption of reasonableness; adequate § 3553(a) consideration on the record

outline.description: Applies the chapter’s doctrines through hypotheticals and offers practical guidance for trial and sentencing advocacy in felon-in-possession cases.
subtopics: Hypo: Prior sighting of the firearm occurs months earlier—intrinsic or Rule 404(b)? Draft the motion and proposed limiting instruction
Hypo: Declarant does not testify—police ‘context’ testimony and Confrontation Clause implications
Hypo: ‘In connection with’ where the other felony is a domestic assault without a separate charge—what evidence suffices?
Authenticating impeachment: securing adoption of interview notes; calling the report author; using recordings
Sentencing advocacy: objecting to PSR factual assertions; marshaling evidence against § 2K2.1(b)(6)(B); framing § 3553(a) mitigation
Preservation checklists: contemporaneous objections, offers of proof, and targeted requests for limiting instructions

outline.description: Assesses Cutbank’s place in the doctrinal landscape and anticipates areas of continued litigation in firearms evidence and sentencing.
subtopics: Reinforcement of Eighth Circuit trends on intrinsic firearm-possession evidence and authentication rigor
Continued vitality of ‘in connection with’ enhancement across non-drug felonies
Appellate deference to within-Guidelines sentences and the strategic importance of undisputed PSRs
Potential friction points: evolving Second Amendment challenges; scope of intrinsic evidence; limits of ‘context’ testimony
Policy considerations: proportionality under ACCA and robust use of uncharged conduct at sentencing
